Personality aspects and intelligence were assessed in a sample of French-Canadian adults from real-life assessment settings (n = 213).
decisions.reason: The paper collects and analyzes data from a new sample of French-Canadian adults (n = 213) to re-test a previously published empirical finding, making its record type a replication.

decisions.quote: This replication and extension of DeYoung, Quilty, Peterson and Gray’s (2014) study aimed to assess the unique variance of each of the 10 aspects of the Big Five personality traits (DeYoung, Quilty & Peterson, 2007) associated to intelligence and its dimensions. Personality aspects and intelligence were assessed in a sample of French-Canadian adults from real-life assessment settings (n = 213). Results showed that the Intellect aspect was independently associated to g, verbal and nonverbal intelligence while its counterpart Openness was independently related to verbal intelligence only, thus replicating the results of the original study.
decisions.reason: Because DeYoung, Quilty, and Peterson (2007) is a background taxonomy citation rather than a tested original and this duplicate row is removed in favor of row 33 (which covers DeYoung et al., 2014), no replication outcome is applicable to this row.
